title: How CERBERUS connects images to a language model
pipelineLabel: Pipeline, left to right. Select a box for details.

pipeline.name: Image encoder
pipeline.text: A frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 turns the image into patch features, and it is never trained.

pipeline.name: Question-aware patch selector
pipeline.text: This does not exist yet: it is a research proposal for a small module that reads the question and decides how many image patches reach the language model.

pipeline.name: Attention pooling
pipeline.text: A learned attention pooling layer squeezes the image features into one vector in the shared space.

pipeline.name: Shared 4096-dimension space
pipeline.text: Images and text land in one shared space of 4096 dimensions, nested so the first 512 or 128 dimensions can be used on their own.

pipeline.name: Qwen decoder with LoRA
pipeline.text: A Qwen decoder with LoRA reads the aligned tokens; there is one 7B run with training loss only and no held-out answer metric yet.

side.name: Text encoder
side.text: A frozen sentence encoder embeds captions, and its output is aligned to the image side.

side.name: Contrastive alignment
side.text: An InfoNCE loss on PixMo image-caption pairs pulls matching images and captions together in the shared space.

side.name: Perceiver compression
side.text: Compressing image tokens with a Perceiver was tried, but retrieval stayed near random, so it is not part of the working path.

detailDefault: Select any box to read what it does and how far it got.

shrink.label: Embedding size
shrink.metric: image-to-text recall@5, paired PixMo validation set, early measurement
shrink.note: The vector is sliced to its first dimensions and renormalised, with no extra parameters.
shrink.caption: This shrinks the vector, not the number of patches. Choosing patches from the question is the proposed next step.
